property_summary: The transfer function always returns true when it completes without reverting.
If transfer succeeds (no revert), the return value is the same as the boolean result of the last call to caddress.call.
When transfer does not revert, the return value equals the boolean result of the first internal call to caddress.call.
The transfer function always returns true when it completes without reverting.
When transfer completes without revert, the return value is true.
For any call to transfer, the return value is always true.
For any call to transfer, the call does not revert.
The transfer function always succeeds (does not revert) when the caller is the contract itself.
The transfer function always returns true when it does not revert.
After a successful transfer, the sum of balances of all addresses involved in the transfer does not decrease.
The transfer function returns true only when the underlying token transferFrom calls succeed for all recipients.
The transfer function should return false when any token transfer fails, but the buggy version always returns true.
The transfer function returns false when any underlying token transfer call fails, but the mutant always returns true.
The transfer function returns true when all underlying transferFrom calls succeed, and reverts when any call fails; the buggy version always returns true even if calls fail.
The transfer function returns false when any underlying token transfer call fails, but the buggy version always returns true.
After calling transfer, the result of the second call to transfer with the same parameters is also true.
Calling transfer does not revert for any valid inputs
Calling transfer does not revert when the inputs are valid.
Calling transfer with the same arguments twice returns the same result both times.
A call to transfer(...) does not revert.
transfer must perform exactly one call per recipient in the input array, so returning true without looping breaks the invariant that each to entry is credited.
After calling transfer, the contract must have made at least as many external calls as the length of the _tos array.
After calling transfer, the sum of external calls made by the contract equals the length of the _tos array.
After calling transfer, the total number of external calls made by the contract equals the length of the _tos array.
After transfer, the contract must have made at least one external call to the caddress if the _tos array has length > 0.
